title: Oriental Phlebotominae: species and subspecies
description: The standard key to all Oriental species known in 1978 (199 couplets). Females and males are separated inside each subgenus. Start here for Thai material, then check the update notes for later splits.

title: Indo-Chinese species (Thailand to Viet Nam)
region: Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Viet Nam, S. China
description: Short key to the 13+ species known from Indo-China in 1962. Older names are converted to current names in the result column.

title: Sri Lanka: females
description: Modern photo-illustrated key to the 22 species recorded from Sri Lanka, females.

title: Sri Lanka: males
description: Modern photo-illustrated key to the species recorded from Sri Lanka, males.

title: Subgenera of Phlebotomus
description: Key to the 11 subgenera of Phlebotomus recognised by Lewis (1982).

title: Idiophlebotomus species
description: Key to the cave-dwelling Idiophlebotomus (now a genus), including I. longiforceps recorded in Thai caves.

title: Euphlebotomus species (argentipes group)
description: Key to Euphlebotomus, the subgenus of the kala-azar vector P. argentipes. Species described later (P. barguesae, P. mascomai, P. seowpohi) are not included.

title: Anaphlebotomus species (stantoni group)
description: Key to Anaphlebotomus. See P. shadenae (2023) for the Thai species close to P. stantoni.

title: Grassomyia: females
description: Female key to all Grassomyia, showing the two Oriental taxa.

title: Sergentomyia babu series: females
description: Female key to the four taxa with a notch at the hind end of the cibarial dental area.

title: Italy (comparison key)
description: Illustrated key to the eight Italian species. Included as a Mediterranean comparison and a model of clear illustration.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: subgenera of Phlebotomus
description: Flowchart key to the Phlebotomus subgenera of the Mediterranean and Middle East (Akhoundi et al. 2025), including Artemievus (P. alexandri). Males by gonostyle spines and gonocoxite basal lobe, females by spermatheca.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Phlebotomus (Phlebotomus) males
description: Males of P. bergeroti, P. duboscqi, P. papatasi and P. salehi.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Phlebotomus (Phlebotomus) females
description: Females of the same four species; P. papatasi and P. duboscqi are not separated. Read the note on couplet 2.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Artemievus and Paraphlebotomus males
description: Males of P. alexandri (Artemievus) and 11 Paraphlebotomus species.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Artemievus and Paraphlebotomus females
description: Females of P. alexandri and Paraphlebotomus; several results are groups of species.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Larroussius males
description: Males of 18 Larroussius taxa; P. major, P. neglectus and P. syriacus are not separated.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Larroussius females
description: Females of Larroussius, mainly by the spermathecal ducts.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Adlerius males
description: Males of 13 Adlerius species by ascoid formula and gonocoxite hairs. Females cannot be separated.

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Transphlebotomus males
description: Males of five Transphlebotomus species (not P. simonahalepae).

title: Mediterranean & Middle East: Transphlebotomus females
description: Females of five Transphlebotomus species (not P. killicki).

title: Laos karst (Vientiane): females
description: Key to females of 19 species from karstic limestone caves of Vientiane Province, Laos (Vongphayloth et al. 2024, Table 4), including Se. dvoraki and Se. marolii. Couplet 9b corrected (printed goto 11); couplets 16-18 are doubtful, see the notes.

title: Laos karst (Vientiane): males
description: Short key to males from karstic limestone areas of Vientiane Province, Laos (Vongphayloth et al. 2024, Table 5). Sergentomyia males are keyed to genus only.
